title: Introduce silk-bridge stall-mitigator and conservative SLO admission (hotfix)
author: Maya Reynolds
description:
Motivation: We observed recurring SLO spikes during rapid regional failovers triggered by transient egress congestion. Root cause analysis showed two contributing factors: (1) the admission controller aggressively replays queued requests during short reconnect windows, and (2) the circuit flip logic reopens too quickly when KV pressure is still settling, causing rapid oscillation and downstream queuing. This PR implements a conservative admission policy ('soft-admit/leanback') and a new stall-mitigation bridge we call 'silk-bridge' to reduce cross-region surge while preserving graceful degradation.

What this PR changes (summary): (a) soft-admit admission controller: instead of immediately draining queued requests after a region rejoin, we apply a configurable linear ramp with jitter to the admitted rate for the first N seconds, driven by observed KV sync progress and per-node token pressure metrics; (b) stall-timer for circuits: introduce a cooldown timer that prevents immediate circuit reopen for a minimum window unless explicit healthy probes pass; (c) silk-bridge fallback: when a region signals persistent KV lag, requests are rerouted to a warm standby region with 'KV-hint' metadata that preserves eventual KV continuity without aggressive replays (best-effort hinting, not a hard migration); (d) telemetry and alerts: new metrics (admission.ramp_pct, silk_bridge.routed, stall_timer.cooldown_seconds) and a lightweight SLO guard that suppresses automated rollouts if 5xx rates increase >2x during the ramp.

Why this is a hotfix: the fix is conservative, low-risk, and addresses an on-call incident (SUP-1984) where customers experienced intermittent latency spikes and retries during a brief multi-zone egress issue. The changes avoid bulk draining and limit cross-region burst amplification.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged by default (feature.silk_bridge.enabled=false). Rollout steps: enable in canary on dedicated-01 for 30m -> monitor admission.ramp_pct and p50/p95 latency for 10m -> enable in regional staging for 1hr with increased telemetry retention -> global enable with slow ramp (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%). If 5xxs or token cost regresses beyond thresholds abort and revert via the flag.

Testing: unit tests for admission ramp and stall timer added; integration harness includes a synthetic egress congestion scenario that validates silk-bridge routing and KV-hint tagging; added a canary test that runs a failover sequence in the perf-lab.

Operational notes: On severe KV lag silk-bridge opts for routing at reduced concurrency (configurable default = 0.25 of normal concurrency) and attaches a header x-silk-bridge:1 to routed requests for downstream observability. There is also an emergency toggle to force immediate drain behavior (feature.admission.immediate_drain=true) for legacy behavior in debugging.

Documentation: Added a short section to the runbooks (internal link: Linear ENG-4217) describing expected telemetry signals and rollback triggers.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration scenario for egress congestion
- [x] Telemetry hooks and alerts
- [x] Feature flag gating
- [x] On-call runbook update

Related: SUP-1984 (support case), ENG-4217 (Linear), and follow-up RFC planned for a more general admission controller rewrite.

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice conservative approach. Two questions: how do we guarantee no request reordering once silk-bridge is used? (author reply below)

Maya Reynolds: Reply: silk-bridge attaches KV-hint metadata; the downstream router treats hints as best-effort and does not surface reordering guarantees. We explicitly document that silk-bridge is a soft fallback and app-level idempotency is still recommended.
Priya Khanna: Please add an explicit test for the cooldown timer preventing reopen during partial KV sync (left a TODO).
Maya Reynolds: Added test in integration-tests and a unit test for stall_timer; expanded comments to describe probe gating.
Liam O'Connor: CI flaked on python lint in first run; reran and green. Approving after green runs.
Diego Ramos: Approved with comments (minor naming nit in controller.go).
merge_result: Squash and merge performed after CI green and two approvals. Merge commit message: 'hotfix(silk-bridge): conservative admission + stall timer to mitigate failover stalls (SUP-1984)'.
release_notes: Hotfix: conservative admission ramp + stall cooldown timer + silk-bridge soft fallback to reduce SLO spikes during regional failovers. Feature-flagged; off by default.
notes_for_oncall: If you see silk_bridge.routed > 0 and p95 latency regressing: flip feature.silk_bridge.enabled=false and watch admission.ramp_pct go to 0. If circuits are sticky after a failover, check stall_timer.cooldown_seconds and health probe success rate. SUP-1984 runbook updated in runbooks/pg-recovery.md.
